crossref.title: Spatially resolved, highly multiplexed RNA profiling in single cells
crossref.publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)
crossref.abstract:
Multiplexed RNA imaging in single cells
                  
                    The basis of cellular function is where and when proteins are expressed and in what quantities. Single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization (smFISH) experiments quantify the copy number and location of mRNA molecules; however, the numbers of RNA species that can be simultaneously measured by smFISH has been limited. Using combinatorial labeling with error-robust encoding schemes, Chen
                    et al.
                    simultaneously imaged 100 to 1000 RNA species in a single cell. Such large-scale detection allows regulatory interactions to be analyzed at the transcriptome scale.
                  
                  
                    Science
                    , this issue p.
                    10.1126/science.aaa6090
